top_signals.title: Gold Tumbles After Fed’s Warsh Comments on Inflation Trend
top_signals.summary: Gold slid the most since July as Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh’s pledge to fight inflation bolstered bets that the US central bank will raise interest rates this year, a headwind for the precious metal.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Fed's Warsh Leads Central Bankers on Walk at Jackson Hole
top_signals.summary: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh leads fellow central bankers, Andrew Bailey, from the Bank of England, and Tiff Macklem, from the Bank of Canada, on a traditional walk at the Fed's annual gathering in Jackson Hole, Wyoming.  (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Central-bank repricing affecting yields, FX, liquidity and equities.

top_signals.title: Warsh’s Hawkish Message Lands as Real Yields Lead Bond Moves
top_signals.summary:
A clear signal that bond markets see credibility in the Federal Reserve’s inflation stance is the jump in real yields, which is outpacing that of nominal and breakeven rates.
Bloomberg 'Odd Lots' podcast hosts Tracy Alloway and Joe Weisenthal discuss Kevin Warsh's debut Jackson Hole speech as Fed Chair. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: PaperCut warns of NG, MF flaw exploited in zero-day attacks
top_signals.summary: PaperCut is warning that hackers are actively exploiting a vulnerability in all versions of its PaperCut NG and PaperCut MF print management software in zero-day attacks. [...]

top_signals.title: Chinese rescue workers reach border crossing destroyed by Himalayan flood
top_signals.summary: Rescue efforts resume after being suspended over fears of further flooding near the Tibet-Nepal border

top_signals.title: 68-year-old imprisoned after making $1.3 million by pirating IPTV services
top_signals.summary: A 68-year-old has been sentenced in the U.K. to more than six years in prison for operating an illegal IPTV (Internet Protocol Television) service that generated £980,812 ($1.3 million) over three years. [...]
